html:
A port city on the Syrian coast near modern Latakia, rich from trade between about 1450 and 1185 BCE. Its archives show the busy Bronze Age world that linked Egypt, the Hittites, Cyprus, Mesopotamia and the Aegean.

Ugarit was a small kingdom under first Egyptian and then Hittite overlords. Its merchants dealt in copper from Cyprus, grain, dyed cloth, timber and pottery from Mycenaean Greece. Scribes wrote letters and contracts in Akkadian cuneiform and several other languages.

They also wrote the local language in an alphabet of 30 cuneiform signs, one of the earliest alphabets, related to the Phoenician alphabet that came later. Its poems about the gods El and Baal shed light on the Canaanite world behind the Hebrew Bible.

The city was destroyed around 1185 BCE in the Late Bronze Age collapse. Its last letters speak of enemy ships raiding the coast, often blamed on the Sea Peoples. A farmer found a tomb there in 1928, and French digs began the next year.
sum: A port city on the Syrian coast near modern Latakia, rich from trade between about 1450 and 1185 BCE. Its archives show the busy Bronze Age world that linked Egypt, the Hittites, Cyprus, Mesopotamia and the Aegean.
